story_type: floatplane crash on a mountainside, 11 survivors hoisted
hook: A floatplane hit a mountain with 11 people aboard.
narration: A floatplane crashed into the side of a mountain in Alaska, with eleven people aboard.
It came down on Mount Jumbo, on Prince of Wales Island, about two thousand feet up.
[short pause] All eleven survived the crash. Now they had to get off the mountain.
A Jayhawk crew from Air Station Sitka hovered over the wreck, working with the Ketchikan Volunteer Rescue Squad and Alaska State Troopers.
The pilots can't see straight down, so the flight mechanic at the door talks them into position and runs the hoist.
The first survivor rode the basket up to the door.
Then it went back down, again and again.
outcome: The Sitka crew hoisted all eleven survivors off the mountain.

location_card.place: Mount Jumbo, Prince of Wales Island, Alaska

title: Floatplane hit a mountain, all 11 lived
description:
On July 10, 2018, a Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Air Station Sitka hoisted all 11 survivors of a floatplane crash from about 2,000 feet up Mount Jumbo, on Prince of Wales Island, Alaska.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Sitka, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/613455/coast-guard-rescues-11-plane-crash-near-ketchikan-alaska
